brief:
“蓝色浪潮”预期成为今日市场的主导变量。随着民主党在参议院拿下关键席位并有望控制众议院，纳指期货与美元走低，亚洲股市跌至六个多月低点，韩国 Kospi 因芯片股抛售明显下挫，投资者担心 AI 行业将面临更严格监管。中国方面，私人调查显示服务业活动意外放缓至三个月低点，企业信心走弱、售价下调而投入成本上升，内需修复仍不稳固。大宗商品与并购同样活跃：布伦特原油在周一暴跌近8%后继续下跌至每桶102.84美元，京东22亿欧元收购德国 Ceconomy 获欧盟批准，沙特阿美利润大增，新加坡股市则因银行盈利前景转弱而走向回调。

1. **“蓝色浪潮”引发 AI 股抛售，亚洲股市创半年新低** — 民主党胜选预期升温，市场担忧 AI 监管收紧，芯片股首当其冲。 [链接](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-04/asian-stocks-fall-as-democratic-gains-in-us-add-to-ai-worries)
2. **纳指期货下挫，AI 板块承压** — 民主党有望拿下众议院，被视为对共和党大金主与 AI 相关股票的潜在打击。 [链接](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-04/us-equity-futures-inch-higher-as-investors-await-midterm-results)
3. **中国服务业景气意外放缓至三个月低点** — 企业信心减弱、售价下调，投入成本却在上升，显示需求端仍偏弱。 [链接](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-04/china-services-gauge-unexpectedly-dips-for-first-time-since-july)
4. **油价延续跌势，布伦特报102.84美元** — 美伊外交进展的报道缓解供应担忧，油价在周一大跌后继续走低。 [链接](https://www.ftchinese.com/story/001111278)
5. **京东22亿欧元收购德国 Ceconomy 获批** — 这是首笔受欧盟《外国补贴条例》评估的中资收购欧洲公司交易，京东承诺补救补贴造成的市场扭曲。 [链接](https://www.ftchinese.com/story/001111277)

items.title: Temasek’s Mapletree Is Said to Pick Banks for Singapore IPO
items.summary: Mapletree Investments Pte, a real estate firm owned by Singapore state investor Temasek Holdings Pte, has picked banks for an initial public offering of parts of the company in the city state that could raise at least S$1 billion ($780 million), according to people familiar with the matter.

items.title: Nasdaq Futures Drop as Signs of ‘Blue-nami’ Weigh on AI Complex
items.summary: US equity index futures continued to push lower Tuesday night as Democrats notched key wins in the Senate and are projected to take control of the US House of Representatives, a potential blow to Republican mega donors like Elon Musk and his companies as regulatory risks grow for AI-linked stocks.

items.title: Asian Stocks Fall as Democratic Gains in US Add to AI Worries
items.summary: Asian stocks fell to their lowest in over six months after early victories by the Democrats in the US midterm elections fueled concerns about tighter oversight of the artificial intelligence industry.

items.title: China Services Gauge Unexpectedly Dips for First Time Since July
items.summary: China’s services activity unexpectedly grew at a slower rate for the first time since July, a private survey showed, as business confidence eased and firms lowered their selling prices despite intensifying inflation in input costs.

items.title: Stocks Slide With Dollar on Rising Blue-Wave Bets: Markets Wrap
items.summary: The growing prospect of a Democratic sweep of Congress rippled across global markets, sending US stock-index futures and the dollar lower while boosting Treasuries as early election returns threatened to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda.

items.title: Can India’s Debt-Fueled Spending Survive Higher Rates?
items.summary:
India’s household borrowing surged 36% in a year, raising questions about how much consumer spending is being powered by debt and whether that growth can last as interest rates rise. Ruchi Bhatia explains.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Florida Passes Property Tax Cuts in Challenge for Local Funding
items.summary: Florida voters passed sweeping property tax cuts in Tuesday’s election, a move that will gut local government funding.

items.title: South Korea’s AI Darlings Become Big Casualty of US Midterm Vote
items.summary: South Korea’s Kospi Index slid as shares of chipmakers plunged on concern that a strong showing by Democrats in the US midterms would lead to greater scrutiny of the artificial intelligence industry.

items.title: Singapore Stocks Set for Correction as Bank Profit Outlook Sours
items.summary: Singapore’s equity benchmark Straits Times Index is on track for a correction as heavyweight bank shares slide on concerns over the outlook for profits.

items.title: Japan Courier Service Yamato’s Shares Surge on Farallon Stake
items.summary: Yamato Holdings Co. shares rallied the most in 18 years after Farallon Capital Management LLC, one of the most prolific activist funds in Japan, reported a stake in the Japanese company and called for a management shakeup.

items.title: Once a Haven for Guerrillas, Venezuela Now Helps U.S. Attack Them
items.summary: Venezuela’s government, which sheltered rebels for decades, cooperated in a recent deadly drone strike as Washington and Caracas forge closer military ties.

items.summary: Oil futures settled lower in a choppy session, with concerns about U.S. strikes on Iranian targets cushioned by continued diplomatic efforts to bring the U.S. and Iran to a conflict settlement.
